evidence.source: CUHK Humanum 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 形義通解
evidence.text: Early forms combine a person with a tree, representing rest in its shade. The person backs toward the trunk. Some tree tops bend toward the person to emphasize shelter; this resembles 禾 but remains 木.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字構形資料庫
evidence.field: 字形演變; 甲骨文合集8159; 金文集成04140; 說文小篆; graph analysis
evidence.text: The catalog lists 休 in an oracle-bone example (合集8159), a bronze example (集成04140), and the Shuowen seal-script category. Its analysis identifies the left element as a person in profile and the right as 木 ‘tree’, interpreting the graph as a person leaning against a tree to rest. These are catalog identifications and an interpretation; I did not independently verify the artifacts’ dates, inscription readings, or contexts.
evidence.title: 漢字「休」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, CUHK Humanum
evidence.field: 形義通解; early forms and graph analysis
evidence.text: The entry analyzes oracle-bone and bronze forms as 人 plus 木, with the person’s back against the tree trunk. It says some tree tops lean toward the person to suggest shade, and distinguishes the shape from 禾 despite their resemblance. This scholarly interpretation supports a person-resting-under-a-tree account, but does not independently establish the reading and motivation of each inscription.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

evidence.field: 休; 字形 and interpretation
evidence.text: This account disputes the person-resting-by-a-tree analysis. It proposes that the 木-like element was originally 禾-shaped and represented paired marker posts at a military gate; 休 then referred to recognizing military merit before them. It cites a bronze inscription phrase glossed ‘good/commendable.’ The page also reports Guo Moruo’s distinct rest-in-a-field proposal and criticizes it. The inspected page presents the competing explanations but does not settle the original graph motivation.
evidence.title: 休(キュウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, CUHK Humanum
evidence.field: 形義通解; cited lexical and inscription uses
evidence.text: The entry proposes a path from tree shade to shelter/protection, then to benefaction or reward; it also associates rest under shade with pleasure and goodness, and resting with stopping. It cites bronze-inscription examples including 剌鼎, 效卣, 員鼎, 師酉簋 and 噩侯鼎, as well as received texts such as 詩經 and 漢書. These attestations illustrate several uses but do not establish their securely dated order or prove every proposed semantic link. The entry says 茠 differentiated the shade sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 as transcribed by 漢典
evidence.field: 休; 說文解字; transmitted definition and analysis
evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen defines 休 as ‘cease/rest’ (息止也), explains the graph as 从人依木 (‘from a person relying on a tree/wood’), and records 庥 as an alternate form with 广. This is a historical lexicographic explanation, not direct proof of the graph’s original motivation.
evidence.title: 休 xiū、xù、xǔ — 漢典

evidence.field: 休 詳細解釋; cited textual examples
evidence.text: The entry cites 《詩·周南·漢廣》 ‘南有喬木，不可休思’ and 《詩·大雅·民勞》 ‘汔可小休’ for rest, and 《詩·大雅·瞻卬》 ‘婦無公事，休其蠶織’ for stopping. It also lists shelter/protection in a note to 《漢書·王莽傳》. These are cited uses in received texts; the dictionary examples do not independently date composition or establish the senses’ chronology.
evidence.title: 休 xiū、xù、xǔ — 漢典

evidence.field: 音系簡文; Mandarin and historical reading summaries
evidence.text: The dictionary gives modern Mandarin xiū and lists Middle Chinese 曉母尤韻平聲, 休小韻, 許尤切, alongside Huang Kan and Wang Li Old Chinese system labels for 休. These readings concern 休; the inspected analyses treat 人 and 木 as semantic components, not sound components, so no component-to-host sound match is proposed.
evidence.title: 休 xiū、xù、xǔ — 漢典

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 形義通解; graph components and cited uses
evidence.text: The entry analyzes early 休 as 人 plus 木, with the person turned back toward the tree. It reads the graph as resting in the tree’s shade, and says some tree tops lean toward the person to suggest shade; despite resemblance, that part is 木, not 禾. It cites the received 《詩·周南·漢廣》 line ‘南有喬木，不可休思’ for resting under a tree, and gives further proposed extensions: shade, protection, royal favor or reward, goodness, pleasure, and stopping. These cited examples do not by themselves establish the order of senses or a securely dated semantic chain.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

evidence.field: 字形; competing formation analysis
evidence.text: The entry disputes the person-resting-by-a-tree explanation. It proposes that the right side was originally 禾-shaped and represented paired marker posts at a military gate; it interprets 休 as recognition or commendation of military merit before them. It cites a bronze-inscription use of 休 meaning ‘good/commendable’ and reports Guo Moruo’s separate rest-in-a-field proposal, which it criticizes. This is a competing scholarly account, not a settled reading of the graph’s original motivation.
evidence.title: 休(キュウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 說文; transmitted definition and Middle Chinese reading
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the transmitted 說文 account ‘息止也。从人依木。’ and lists 許尤切 with Middle Chinese 曉母、尤韻、平聲. This records a historical lexicographic explanation and rhyme-book classification; it does not independently establish the graph’s original motivation or the chronology of lexical senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 形義通解; lexical sense examples
evidence.text: The entry cites bronze-inscription examples for protection/favor, reward, goodness, and stopping, including 剌鼎、效卣、員鼎、師酉簋 and 噩侯鼎. It also cites received texts including 《漢書》 and 《詩經》. It proposes semantic connections among shade, protection, favor or reward, goodness and pleasure, and rest or stopping, but gives no independently verified absolute dates for those individual inscriptions here. The bronze examples therefore indicate reported uses, not a demonstrated earliest-sense sequence.

evidence.source: Taiwan Academic Online Journal Platform; 張宇衛
evidence.field: Article abstract; Zhou bronze inscription senses
evidence.text: The 2026 article abstract classifies Zhou bronze uses into six syntactic and lexical groups: giving/receiving commendation, commendation as a noun, praising, beautifying, a metonymic utensil sense, and virtuous/good as an adjective. This supports several early bronze uses beyond ‘rest’; the abstract does not provide individual artifact dates or establish a chronological semantic chain.
evidence.title: 談兩周金文「休」字文例結構與義項 / On the Textual Structures and Word Senses of the Character “Xiū” in Bronze Inscriptions from the Zhou Dynasties

It also repeats the traditional person-and-tree explanation; the citations do not independently date the composition of those texts or determine sense order.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

The person-plus-tree/shade account and the military marker-post/commendation account remain in material disagreement. The inspected sources do not settle the original graph motivation; no inscription image or primary artifact catalog entry was independently inspected visually.

Earliest attested lexical sense cannot be ranked securely from the consulted pages. Dictionary-cited received texts and bronze examples were not independently dated or checked in their primary contexts; do not infer chronology from gloss ordering.

CUHK’s proposed links among shade, protection, royal favor, reward, goodness, pleasure, resting and stopping are plausible source interpretations, but the evidence inspected here does not independently establish each semantic bridge or its order.

The official Unicode Unihan record for U+4F11 returned an internal error, so current kMandarin was not independently verified. No sound component or whole-graph phonetic loan is proposed in the consulted analyses; no component-to-host ancient sound comparison is warranted.

The exact Xiaoxuetang 休 query record/image could not be retrieved. Commons file-description results were visible, but page opens failed with cache misses, preventing safe extraction of a direct original image URL. No candidate meets the direct-image-link requirement, so the glyph list is empty.

The person-and-tree explanation is the commonly cataloged account; Kotobank’s military gate and commendation proposal materially disputes the right-hand component and motivation. Neither inspected account settles the original meaning decisively.

Catalogs identify oracle-bone and bronze examples, including Heji 8159 and Jicheng 4140, but primary artifact photographs/rubbings and inscription contexts were not independently inspected here. The exact earliest written lexical sense and artifact dates therefore remain unsettled.

The 2026 article abstract offers a syntactic sense taxonomy for Western Zhou bronze occurrences, including commendation and goodness senses; its full text was not accessed, and the abstract does not prove development from these senses to rest, shelter, favor, or stopping.

Dictionary quotations from received texts attest rest and stop in cited passages but do not independently date textual composition or establish semantic chronology. Reported links among shade, protection, favor, merit, goodness, pleasure, rest, and cessation remain partly interpretive.
